expected: The default run passes its step with a "differs" verdict recorded, and the run configured to fail does fail — most visual differences are intentional, and a check that fails the build on every redesign is one a team switches off
detail: default: run passed, verdict differs; onDifference=fail: run failed, verdict differs

objective: A difference stores the baseline, the capture and a diff; a match stores none
preconditions: a baseline, and a page that has visibly changed
input: A matching run and a differing run
expected: Three image keys on the difference and none on the match — the images are the whole point of a visual failure, and three per passing step is a storage bill for pictures nobody opens
detail: match: no images stored; differs: baseline=true actual=true diff=true

objective: A run with no visual step reports the metric as unmeasured, never as zero
preconditions: a gate rule on visual differences, and a run that compares nothing
input: A run of a test with no checkVisual step
expected: The rule is reported as not measured and sent for review — a rule that passed because nothing looked reads as "the page is unchanged"
detail: rule measured=false passed=false; outcome review

objective: Masking a region that changes every run removes the difference entirely
preconditions: the page renders a live timestamp whose digits change on every request
input: Repeated runs with the timestamp masked
expected: Exactly zero differing pixels, and the masked selector recorded in the result — masking the region that keeps failing is the obvious way to make a visual check useless while appearing to run it, so what was hidden is on the record
detail: two masked comparisons: 0 and 0 differing pixels; recorded as masked: ["[data-testid=\"generated-at\"]"]

objective: A baseline taken at one viewport is not compared against another
preconditions: a baseline taken at 1280 wide
input: The same check run again at 800 wide
expected: A new baseline rather than a difference — a baseline at 1280 says nothing about how the page looks at 800, and comparing across them would report a difference on every run until somebody switched the check off
detail: 1280: newBaseline then match; 800 with the same baseline name: newBaseline

objective: The scope guard refuses no scope at all
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: no scope at all
expected: Refused with scopeMissing. The absence of a restriction is not permission. An application nobody has authorized security testing against gets nothing.
detail: scopeMissing: This application has no security scope. Nobody has authorized security testing against it, and the absence of a restriction is not permission.

objective: The scope guard refuses scope disabled
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved

expected: Refused with scopeDisabled. A scope that exists but is switched off permits nothing.

input: no written authorization
expected: Refused with scopeMissing. Authorization is a written statement by a person, not a default.

objective: The scope guard refuses empty domain allowlist

input: empty domain allowlist
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. An empty allowlist permits nothing. Treating it as "no restriction" is how a scanner ends up on the internet.
detail: domainNotAllowed: The scope names no allowed domains. An empty allowlist permits nothing.

objective: The scope guard refuses a host nobody authorized

expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. Arbitrary URLs are never allowed.

objective: The scope guard refuses GCP metadata by name

objective: The scope guard refuses no scope at all
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: no scope at all
expected: Refused with scopeMissing. The absence of a restriction is not permission. An application nobody has authorized security testing against gets nothing.
detail: scopeMissing: This application has no security scope. Nobody has authorized security testing against it, and the absence of a restriction is not permission.

objective: The scope guard refuses scope disabled
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: scope disabled
expected: Refused with scopeDisabled. A scope that exists but is switched off permits nothing.
detail: scopeDisabled: The security scope exists but is not enabled.

objective: The scope guard refuses no written authorization
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: no written authorization
expected: Refused with scopeMissing. Authorization is a written statement by a person, not a default.
detail: scopeMissing: The security scope carries no written authorization.

objective: The scope guard refuses empty domain allowlist
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: empty domain allowlist
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. An empty allowlist permits nothing. Treating it as "no restriction" is how a scanner ends up on the internet.
detail: domainNotAllowed: The scope names no allowed domains. An empty allowlist permits nothing.

objective: The scope guard refuses a host nobody authorized
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: a host nobody authorized
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. Arbitrary URLs are never allowed.
detail: domainNotAllowed: Host 'example.com' is not in the scope's allowed domains.

objective: The scope guard refuses cloud metadata, despite an allowlist that names it
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: cloud metadata, despite an allowlist that names it
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. Never a legitimate target, whatever the scope says. A scope cannot opt in to this.
detail: domainNotAllowed: '169.254.169.254' is never a legitimate target, whatever the scope allows.

objective: The scope guard refuses GCP metadata by name
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: GCP metadata by name
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. The same, by hostname rather than address.
detail: domainNotAllowed: 'metadata.google.internal' is never a legitimate target, whatever the scope allows.

objective: The scope guard refuses a non-http scheme
preconditions: the guard evaluated directly, with no application involved
input: a non-http scheme
expected: Refused with domainNotAllowed. Only http and https are ever issued.
detail: domainNotAllowed: Scheme 'file:' is not permitted.

objective: The scope guard refuses a blocked path

input: a blocked path
expected: Refused with pathBlocked. A path the owner excluded stays excluded.

objective: The scope guard refuses a path outside the allowlist

input: a path outside the allowlist

objective: The scope guard refuses active testing when the scope permits passive only

expected: Refused with activeTestingNotAllowed. Passive means passive.
detail: activeTestingNotAllowed: The scope does not permit active testing.

objective: The scope guard refuses a DELETE under an ordinary scope

objective: The scope guard refuses a POST declared passive

objective: The scope guard refuses production, allowed by the scope but not authorized for this run

objective: The scope guard refuses a different environment from the one authorized

objective: The measured detection and false-positive rates are recorded, not claimed
preconditions: every detection and precision scenario has run
input: 34 scenarios, each run against the flaw and against its correction
expected: Every scenario detects its flaw and none reports it when corrected. The numbers are the ones this run measured against this lab, and say nothing about any other application
detail: 34/34 detected, 0 false positive(s) on the corrected application

objective: Security scanning against a production environment
expected: Refused unless explicitly authorized for that run
detail: Not executed. Production security testing is disabled by default and no production environment exists here. The refusal path is verified by SECG-016 and SECG-017; the permitted path is not exercised anywhere and is NOT VERIFIED.

objective: Browser-driven DOM XSS detection
expected: A browser-driven scan reaches the sinks a response-only scan cannot
detail: Not implemented. SECX-001 records DOM XSS as not testable by this scan rather than as absent. Until a browser-driven security scan exists, DOM-based XSS is an untested area of coverage.

objective: Detection rate against an application AIRA has not seen
expected: A measured rate that generalises
detail: Not measured, and not measurable here. Every flaw in the lab was written alongside the check that finds it. The rate in SECR-001 describes this lab and nothing else.

objective: A scan that did not run is REVIEW, never a pass
preconditions: no scan
input: Coverage with scanRan false
expected: REVIEW, and a summary that says NOT SCANNED. A build that goes green because nobody scanned is the failure this gate exists to prevent
detail: REVIEW: NOT SCANNED. No security tests were executed for this build, so nothing is known about its security posture from AIRA.

objective: Two real findings from a real scan block the build
preconditions: the access-control lab with BOLA and vertical escalation switched on
input: A live scan, its findings passed to the gate under the default policy
expected: FAIL, naming the two categories — and the findings are the ones the scan actually produced, not a fixture
detail: FAIL; 2 finding(s) [BOLA, BrokenFunctionLevelAuthorization]; Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A clean scan never claims the application is secure
preconditions: the same lab with both flaws corrected
input: A live scan of the corrected application
expected: The sentence the brief requires — "Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests" — and never "secure" or "zero vulnerabilities"
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A partial scan does not pass, however clean it was
preconditions: a scan that ran one of five configured checks and found nothing
input: Clean coverage with one of five checks executed
expected: REVIEW. "Nothing found" from a fifth of a scan describes a fifth of an application
detail: REVIEW: Only 1 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A scan whose scope refused most of its requests does not pass
preconditions: a clean scan in which the scope blocked 80 of 100 requests
input: Clean findings, heavily blocked coverage
expected: REVIEW, naming the proportion refused. Coverage is what a reader needs in order to know what a clean result means
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 80% of the scan's requests were refused by its own scope. The findings describe the part of the application the scan was allowed to reach.

objective: A suppression with no written justification is counted as open and fails the build
preconditions: a real critical finding marked false positive with no reason
input: The scan's BOLA finding, status FalsePositive, justification empty
expected: FAIL. An unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off, and honouring it would make the gate decoration
detail: FAIL: 1 finding(s) are suppressed with no written justification or no named decision-maker. They are counted as open, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off.

objective: A regression fails at any severity
preconditions: a low-severity finding previously recorded as resolved
input: One Low finding with isRegression true
expected: FAIL. Something that was repaired has been undone, and severity is not the question
detail: FAIL: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 security finding(s) that were fixed have come back. A regression fails at any severity: something that was repaired has been undone.

objective: A single unreproduced indicator goes to review rather than stopping the release
preconditions: a new High finding at Low confidence
input: One High/Low finding
expected: REVIEW, not FAIL. A gate that stops a release on one unreproduced signal gets switched off, and then nothing is gated at all
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 new finding(s) at or above High rest on a single unreproduced indicator. A person should look rather than the build stopping.

objective: A finding with no evidence is neither failed nor dismissed
preconditions: a Critical finding carrying no exchange
input: One Critical finding with hasEvidence false
expected: REVIEW. A claim nobody can check is not a finding yet, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 finding(s) carry no evidence. They are neither failed nor dismissed: a claim nobody can check is not yet a finding, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so.

objective: Untested areas appear in the summary of a clean result
preconditions: a clean scan that names what it did not test
input: The corrected scan, whose coverage names DOM XSS and cloud metadata as untested
expected: The summary names them. The brief requires tested coverage to be distinguishable from untested areas, and a clean summary that lists neither invites the reader to assume everything was covered
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A finding reported twice gets the same fingerprint, and a different one does not
preconditions: two findings from the real scan
input: The same finding reworded, and a genuinely different finding
expected: The reworded finding matches; the different one does not. A fingerprint that changed when a title was rephrased would report everything as new every run
detail: same finding reworded: matched; different finding: distinct

objective: A finding absent from a scan is never recorded as resolved on absence alone
preconditions: a baseline with a confirmed finding, and a scan whose check did not run
input: A baseline finding whose check is not in the executed list
expected: notObserved, with the reason. The brief forbids self-healing or anything else hiding a security regression, and calling an unrun check a fix is exactly that
detail: notObserved: The check that found this did not run in this scan, so its absence is not evidence of anything.

objective: A check that ran and did not reproduce a finding says so, and still does not resolve it
preconditions: a baseline finding whose check ran this time and found nothing
input: The same baseline, with authz.bola in the executed list
expected: notReproduced — grounds for a person to mark it resolved, not a resolution
detail: notReproduced: The check that found this ran again and did not reproduce it. That is grounds for a person to mark it resolved; it is not a resolution on its own.

objective: A resolved finding detected again is marked as a regression
preconditions: a baseline in which the real BOLA finding was resolved
input: The live scan compared against that baseline
expected: isRegression true and status Regressed, which the gate then fails at any severity
detail: 2 regression(s); gate FAIL

objective: A triage decision carries forward but the severity does not
preconditions: a baseline finding accepted at Medium, now detected at Critical
input: The same fingerprint with a higher severity in this scan
expected: The acceptance carries forward and the new severity is kept. A flaw that got worse since somebody accepted it should not inherit the old severity along with the decision
detail: status Accepted carried forward; severity Critical (was Medium)

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no justification
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no named decision-maker
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no named decision-maker
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no named decision-maker. Somebody has to be accountable for a finding being set aside.

objective: Triage refuses a justification too short to be one
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a justification too short to be one
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive: the justification is too short to be one. State what was checked and what it showed.

objective: Triage refuses an accepted risk with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: an accepted risk with no justification
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as Accepted with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses an unknown status
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: an unknown status
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Unknown security finding status 'Ignored'.

objective: A properly justified decision is accepted and appended to the history, never overwriting it
preconditions: a confirmed finding, marked a false positive with a reason and a name
input: A justification of substance and a named decision-maker, applied twice
expected: Both decisions in the history with the status each moved from. A status field that holds only the latest answer is not an audit trail
detail: Confirmed → NeedsReview, NeedsReview → FalsePositive

objective: A false positive suppresses that finding and not the same class elsewhere

objective: Self-healing cannot mark a security finding resolved

objective: A scan that did not run is REVIEW, never a pass
preconditions: no scan
input: Coverage with scanRan false
expected: REVIEW, and a summary that says NOT SCANNED. A build that goes green because nobody scanned is the failure this gate exists to prevent
detail: REVIEW: NOT SCANNED. No security tests were executed for this build, so nothing is known about its security posture from AIRA.

objective: Two real findings from a real scan block the build
preconditions: the access-control lab with BOLA and vertical escalation switched on
input: A live scan, its findings passed to the gate under the default policy
expected: FAIL, naming the two categories — and the findings are the ones the scan actually produced, not a fixture
detail: FAIL; 2 finding(s) [BOLA, BrokenFunctionLevelAuthorization]; Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A clean scan never claims the application is secure
preconditions: the same lab with both flaws corrected
input: A live scan of the corrected application
expected: The sentence the brief requires — "Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests" — and never "secure" or "zero vulnerabilities"
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A partial scan does not pass, however clean it was
preconditions: a scan that ran one of five configured checks and found nothing
input: Clean coverage with one of five checks executed
expected: REVIEW. "Nothing found" from a fifth of a scan describes a fifth of an application
detail: REVIEW: Only 1 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A scan whose scope refused most of its requests does not pass
preconditions: a clean scan in which the scope blocked 80 of 100 requests
input: Clean findings, heavily blocked coverage
expected: REVIEW, naming the proportion refused. Coverage is what a reader needs in order to know what a clean result means
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 80% of the scan's requests were refused by its own scope. The findings describe the part of the application the scan was allowed to reach.

objective: A suppression with no written justification is counted as open and fails the build
preconditions: a real critical finding marked false positive with no reason
input: The scan's BOLA finding, status FalsePositive, justification empty
expected: FAIL. An unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off, and honouring it would make the gate decoration
detail: FAIL: 1 finding(s) are suppressed with no written justification or no named decision-maker. They are counted as open, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off.

objective: A regression fails at any severity
preconditions: a low-severity finding previously recorded as resolved
input: One Low finding with isRegression true
expected: FAIL. Something that was repaired has been undone, and severity is not the question
detail: FAIL: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 security finding(s) that were fixed have come back. A regression fails at any severity: something that was repaired has been undone.

objective: A single unreproduced indicator goes to review rather than stopping the release
preconditions: a new High finding at Low confidence
input: One High/Low finding
expected: REVIEW, not FAIL. A gate that stops a release on one unreproduced signal gets switched off, and then nothing is gated at all
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 new finding(s) at or above High rest on a single unreproduced indicator. A person should look rather than the build stopping.

objective: A finding with no evidence is neither failed nor dismissed

input: One Critical finding with hasEvidence false

detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 finding(s) carry no evidence. They are neither failed nor dismissed: a claim nobody can check is not yet a finding, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so.

detail: 34/34 detected, 0 false positive(s) on the corrected application

objective: Security scanning against a production environment
expected: Refused unless explicitly authorized for that run
detail: Not executed. Production security testing is disabled by default and no production environment exists here. The refusal path is verified by SECG-016 and SECG-017; the permitted path is not exercised anywhere and is NOT VERIFIED.

objective: Browser-driven DOM XSS detection
expected: A browser-driven scan reaches the sinks a response-only scan cannot
detail: Not implemented. SECX-001 records DOM XSS as not testable by this scan rather than as absent. Until a browser-driven security scan exists, DOM-based XSS is an untested area of coverage.

objective: Detection rate against an application AIRA has not seen
expected: A measured rate that generalises
detail: Not measured, and not measurable here. Every flaw in the lab was written alongside the check that finds it. The rate in SECR-001 describes this lab and nothing else.

objective: A scan that did not run is REVIEW, never a pass
preconditions: no scan
input: Coverage with scanRan false
expected: REVIEW, and a summary that says NOT SCANNED. A build that goes green because nobody scanned is the failure this gate exists to prevent
detail: REVIEW: NOT SCANNED. No security tests were executed for this build, so nothing is known about its security posture from AIRA.

objective: Two real findings from a real scan block the build
preconditions: the access-control lab with BOLA and vertical escalation switched on
input: A live scan, its findings passed to the gate under the default policy
expected: FAIL, naming the two categories — and the findings are the ones the scan actually produced, not a fixture
detail: FAIL; 2 finding(s) [BOLA, BrokenFunctionLevelAuthorization]; Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A clean scan never claims the application is secure
preconditions: the same lab with both flaws corrected
input: A live scan of the corrected application
expected: The sentence the brief requires — "Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests" — and never "secure" or "zero vulnerabilities"
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A partial scan does not pass, however clean it was
preconditions: a scan that ran one of five configured checks and found nothing
input: Clean coverage with one of five checks executed
expected: REVIEW. "Nothing found" from a fifth of a scan describes a fifth of an application
detail: REVIEW: Only 1 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A scan whose scope refused most of its requests does not pass
preconditions: a clean scan in which the scope blocked 80 of 100 requests
input: Clean findings, heavily blocked coverage
expected: REVIEW, naming the proportion refused. Coverage is what a reader needs in order to know what a clean result means
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 80% of the scan's requests were refused by its own scope. The findings describe the part of the application the scan was allowed to reach.

objective: A suppression with no written justification is counted as open and fails the build
preconditions: a real critical finding marked false positive with no reason
input: The scan's BOLA finding, status FalsePositive, justification empty
expected: FAIL. An unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off, and honouring it would make the gate decoration
detail: FAIL: 1 finding(s) are suppressed with no written justification or no named decision-maker. They are counted as open, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off.

objective: A regression fails at any severity
preconditions: a low-severity finding previously recorded as resolved
input: One Low finding with isRegression true
expected: FAIL. Something that was repaired has been undone, and severity is not the question
detail: FAIL: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 security finding(s) that were fixed have come back. A regression fails at any severity: something that was repaired has been undone.

objective: A single unreproduced indicator goes to review rather than stopping the release
preconditions: a new High finding at Low confidence
input: One High/Low finding
expected: REVIEW, not FAIL. A gate that stops a release on one unreproduced signal gets switched off, and then nothing is gated at all
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 new finding(s) at or above High rest on a single unreproduced indicator. A person should look rather than the build stopping.

objective: A finding with no evidence is neither failed nor dismissed
preconditions: a Critical finding carrying no exchange
input: One Critical finding with hasEvidence false
expected: REVIEW. A claim nobody can check is not a finding yet, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 finding(s) carry no evidence. They are neither failed nor dismissed: a claim nobody can check is not yet a finding, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so.

objective: Untested areas appear in the summary of a clean result
preconditions: a clean scan that names what it did not test
input: The corrected scan, whose coverage names DOM XSS and cloud metadata as untested

detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: The gate can pass — a clean scan with full coverage is a PASS, not a REVIEW
preconditions: the corrected application, with every configured check recorded as executed

detail: notObserved: The check that found this did not run in this scan, so its absence is not evidence of anything.

objective: A check that ran and did not reproduce a finding says so, and still does not resolve it

expected: notReproduced — grounds for a person to mark it resolved, not a resolution
detail: notReproduced: The check that found this ran again and did not reproduce it. That is grounds for a person to mark it resolved; it is not a resolution on its own.

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no named decision-maker

objective: Security scanning against a production environment
expected: Refused unless explicitly authorized for that run
detail: Not executed. Production security testing is disabled by default and no production environment exists here. The refusal path is verified by SECG-016 and SECG-017; the permitted path is not exercised anywhere and is NOT VERIFIED.

objective: Browser-driven DOM XSS detection
expected: A browser-driven scan reaches the sinks a response-only scan cannot
detail: Not implemented. SECX-001 records DOM XSS as not testable by this scan rather than as absent. Until a browser-driven security scan exists, DOM-based XSS is an untested area of coverage.

objective: Detection rate against an application AIRA has not seen
expected: A measured rate that generalises
detail: Not measured, and not measurable here. Every flaw in the lab was written alongside the check that finds it. The rate in SECR-001 describes this lab and nothing else.

objective: A scan that did not run is REVIEW, never a pass
preconditions: no scan
input: Coverage with scanRan false
expected: REVIEW, and a summary that says NOT SCANNED. A build that goes green because nobody scanned is the failure this gate exists to prevent
detail: REVIEW: NOT SCANNED. No security tests were executed for this build, so nothing is known about its security posture from AIRA.

objective: Two real findings from a real scan block the build
preconditions: the access-control lab with BOLA and vertical escalation switched on
input: A live scan, its findings passed to the gate under the default policy
expected: FAIL, naming the two categories — and the findings are the ones the scan actually produced, not a fixture
detail: FAIL; 2 finding(s) [BOLA, BrokenFunctionLevelAuthorization]; Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A clean scan never claims the application is secure
preconditions: the same lab with both flaws corrected
input: A live scan of the corrected application
expected: The sentence the brief requires — "Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests" — and never "secure" or "zero vulnerabilities"
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A partial scan does not pass, however clean it was
preconditions: a scan that ran one of five configured checks and found nothing
input: Clean coverage with one of five checks executed
expected: REVIEW. "Nothing found" from a fifth of a scan describes a fifth of an application
detail: REVIEW: Only 1 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A scan whose scope refused most of its requests does not pass
preconditions: a clean scan in which the scope blocked 80 of 100 requests
input: Clean findings, heavily blocked coverage
expected: REVIEW, naming the proportion refused. Coverage is what a reader needs in order to know what a clean result means
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 80% of the scan's requests were refused by its own scope. The findings describe the part of the application the scan was allowed to reach.

objective: A suppression with no written justification is counted as open and fails the build
preconditions: a real critical finding marked false positive with no reason
input: The scan's BOLA finding, status FalsePositive, justification empty
expected: FAIL. An unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off, and honouring it would make the gate decoration
detail: FAIL: 1 finding(s) are suppressed with no written justification or no named decision-maker. They are counted as open, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off.

objective: A regression fails at any severity
preconditions: a low-severity finding previously recorded as resolved
input: One Low finding with isRegression true
expected: FAIL. Something that was repaired has been undone, and severity is not the question
detail: FAIL: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 security finding(s) that were fixed have come back. A regression fails at any severity: something that was repaired has been undone.

objective: A single unreproduced indicator goes to review rather than stopping the release
preconditions: a new High finding at Low confidence
input: One High/Low finding
expected: REVIEW, not FAIL. A gate that stops a release on one unreproduced signal gets switched off, and then nothing is gated at all
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 new finding(s) at or above High rest on a single unreproduced indicator. A person should look rather than the build stopping.

objective: A finding with no evidence is neither failed nor dismissed
preconditions: a Critical finding carrying no exchange
input: One Critical finding with hasEvidence false
expected: REVIEW. A claim nobody can check is not a finding yet, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 finding(s) carry no evidence. They are neither failed nor dismissed: a claim nobody can check is not yet a finding, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so.

objective: Untested areas appear in the summary of a clean result
preconditions: a clean scan that names what it did not test
input: The corrected scan, whose coverage names DOM XSS and cloud metadata as untested
expected: The summary names them. The brief requires tested coverage to be distinguishable from untested areas, and a clean summary that lists neither invites the reader to assume everything was covered
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: The gate can pass — a clean scan with full coverage is a PASS, not a REVIEW
preconditions: the corrected application, with every configured check recorded as executed
input: The corrected scan's findings with coverage showing all five checks run
expected: PASS. Ten rules that produce REVIEW or FAIL prove only that the gate says no to everything; this is the case that shows it can say yes
detail: PASS; 8/8 rule(s) satisfied

objective: A finding reported twice gets the same fingerprint, and a different one does not
preconditions: two findings from the real scan
input: The same finding reworded, and a genuinely different finding
expected: The reworded finding matches; the different one does not. A fingerprint that changed when a title was rephrased would report everything as new every run
detail: same finding reworded: matched; different finding: distinct

objective: A finding absent from a scan is never recorded as resolved on absence alone
preconditions: a baseline with a confirmed finding, and a scan whose check did not run
input: A baseline finding whose check is not in the executed list
expected: notObserved, with the reason. The brief forbids self-healing or anything else hiding a security regression, and calling an unrun check a fix is exactly that
detail: notObserved: The check that found this did not run in this scan, so its absence is not evidence of anything.

objective: A check that ran and did not reproduce a finding says so, and still does not resolve it
preconditions: a baseline finding whose check ran this time and found nothing
input: The same baseline, with authz.bola in the executed list
expected: notReproduced — grounds for a person to mark it resolved, not a resolution
detail: notReproduced: The check that found this ran again and did not reproduce it. That is grounds for a person to mark it resolved; it is not a resolution on its own.

objective: A resolved finding detected again is marked as a regression
preconditions: a baseline in which the real BOLA finding was resolved
input: The live scan compared against that baseline
expected: isRegression true and status Regressed, which the gate then fails at any severity
detail: 2 regression(s); gate FAIL

objective: A triage decision carries forward but the severity does not
preconditions: a baseline finding accepted at Medium, now detected at Critical
input: The same fingerprint with a higher severity in this scan
expected: The acceptance carries forward and the new severity is kept. A flaw that got worse since somebody accepted it should not inherit the old severity along with the decision
detail: status Accepted carried forward; severity Critical (was Medium)

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no justification
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no named decision-maker
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no named decision-maker
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no named decision-maker. Somebody has to be accountable for a finding being set aside.

objective: Triage refuses a justification too short to be one
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a justification too short to be one
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive: the justification is too short to be one. State what was checked and what it showed.

objective: Triage refuses an accepted risk with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan

expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as Accepted with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses an unknown status

input: an unknown status
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Unknown security finding status 'Ignored'.

preconditions: a confirmed finding, marked a false positive with a reason and a name

objective: A false positive suppresses that finding and not the same class elsewhere

objective: Self-healing cannot mark a security finding resolved
preconditions: the triage workflow
input: An attempt to resolve a finding with no person named

detail: automated suppression refused (Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive: the justification is...); an unreproduced finding stays Confirmed

objective: The measured detection and false-positive rates are recorded, not claimed
preconditions: every detection and precision scenario has run
input: 34 scenarios, each run against the flaw and against its correction
expected: Every scenario detects its flaw and none reports it when corrected. The numbers are the ones this run measured against this lab, and say nothing about any other application
detail: 34/34 detected, 0 false positive(s) on the corrected application

objective: Security scanning against a production environment
expected: Refused unless explicitly authorized for that run
detail: Not executed. Production security testing is disabled by default and no production environment exists here. The refusal path is verified by SECG-016 and SECG-017; the permitted path is not exercised anywhere and is NOT VERIFIED.

objective: Browser-driven DOM XSS detection
expected: A browser-driven scan reaches the sinks a response-only scan cannot
detail: Not implemented. SECX-001 records DOM XSS as not testable by this scan rather than as absent. Until a browser-driven security scan exists, DOM-based XSS is an untested area of coverage.

objective: Detection rate against an application AIRA has not seen
expected: A measured rate that generalises
detail: Not measured, and not measurable here. Every flaw in the lab was written alongside the check that finds it. The rate in SECR-001 describes this lab and nothing else.

objective: A scan that did not run is REVIEW, never a pass
preconditions: no scan
input: Coverage with scanRan false
expected: REVIEW, and a summary that says NOT SCANNED. A build that goes green because nobody scanned is the failure this gate exists to prevent
detail: REVIEW: NOT SCANNED. No security tests were executed for this build, so nothing is known about its security posture from AIRA.

objective: Two real findings from a real scan block the build
preconditions: the access-control lab with BOLA and vertical escalation switched on
input: A live scan, its findings passed to the gate under the default policy
expected: FAIL, naming the two categories — and the findings are the ones the scan actually produced, not a fixture
detail: FAIL; 2 finding(s) [BOLA, BrokenFunctionLevelAuthorization]; Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A clean scan never claims the application is secure
preconditions: the same lab with both flaws corrected
input: A live scan of the corrected application
expected: The sentence the brief requires — "Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests" — and never "secure" or "zero vulnerabilities"
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: A partial scan does not pass, however clean it was
preconditions: a scan that ran one of five configured checks and found nothing
input: Clean coverage with one of five checks executed
expected: REVIEW. "Nothing found" from a fifth of a scan describes a fifth of an application
detail: REVIEW: Only 1 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else.

objective: A scan whose scope refused most of its requests does not pass
preconditions: a clean scan in which the scope blocked 80 of 100 requests
input: Clean findings, heavily blocked coverage
expected: REVIEW, naming the proportion refused. Coverage is what a reader needs in order to know what a clean result means
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 80% of the scan's requests were refused by its own scope. The findings describe the part of the application the scan was allowed to reach.

objective: A suppression with no written justification is counted as open and fails the build
preconditions: a real critical finding marked false positive with no reason
input: The scan's BOLA finding, status FalsePositive, justification empty
expected: FAIL. An unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off, and honouring it would make the gate decoration
detail: FAIL: 1 finding(s) are suppressed with no written justification or no named decision-maker. They are counted as open, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from switching the check off.

objective: A regression fails at any severity
preconditions: a low-severity finding previously recorded as resolved
input: One Low finding with isRegression true
expected: FAIL. Something that was repaired has been undone, and severity is not the question
detail: FAIL: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 security finding(s) that were fixed have come back. A regression fails at any severity: something that was repaired has been undone.

objective: A single unreproduced indicator goes to review rather than stopping the release
preconditions: a new High finding at Low confidence
input: One High/Low finding
expected: REVIEW, not FAIL. A gate that stops a release on one unreproduced signal gets switched off, and then nothing is gated at all
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 new finding(s) at or above High rest on a single unreproduced indicator. A person should look rather than the build stopping.

objective: A finding with no evidence is neither failed nor dismissed
preconditions: a Critical finding carrying no exchange
input: One Critical finding with hasEvidence false
expected: REVIEW. A claim nobody can check is not a finding yet, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so
detail: REVIEW: Only 2 of 5 configured check(s) executed. A result from a partial scan describes the part that ran and nothing else. 1 finding(s) carry no evidence. They are neither failed nor dismissed: a claim nobody can check is not yet a finding, and dropping it silently is worse than saying so.

objective: Untested areas appear in the summary of a clean result
preconditions: a clean scan that names what it did not test
input: The corrected scan, whose coverage names DOM XSS and cloud metadata as untested
expected: The summary names them. The brief requires tested coverage to be distinguishable from untested areas, and a clean summary that lists neither invites the reader to assume everything was covered
detail: Within the configured scope and test coverage, no security findings were detected by the executed AIRA security tests (2 of 5 configured check(s), 7 request(s) issued). This is not a statement that the application is secure or that no vulnerabilities exist. Untested: DOM-based XSS (needs a browser-driven scan); cloud metadata (off by default).

objective: The gate can pass — a clean scan with full coverage is a PASS, not a REVIEW
preconditions: the corrected application, with every configured check recorded as executed
input: The corrected scan's findings with coverage showing all five checks run
expected: PASS. Ten rules that produce REVIEW or FAIL prove only that the gate says no to everything; this is the case that shows it can say yes
detail: PASS; 8/8 rule(s) satisfied

objective: A finding reported twice gets the same fingerprint, and a different one does not
preconditions: two findings from the real scan
input: The same finding reworded, and a genuinely different finding
expected: The reworded finding matches; the different one does not. A fingerprint that changed when a title was rephrased would report everything as new every run
detail: same finding reworded: matched; different finding: distinct

objective: A finding absent from a scan is never recorded as resolved on absence alone
preconditions: a baseline with a confirmed finding, and a scan whose check did not run
input: A baseline finding whose check is not in the executed list
expected: notObserved, with the reason. The brief forbids self-healing or anything else hiding a security regression, and calling an unrun check a fix is exactly that
detail: notObserved: The check that found this did not run in this scan, so its absence is not evidence of anything.

objective: A check that ran and did not reproduce a finding says so, and still does not resolve it
preconditions: a baseline finding whose check ran this time and found nothing
input: The same baseline, with authz.bola in the executed list
expected: notReproduced — grounds for a person to mark it resolved, not a resolution
detail: notReproduced: The check that found this ran again and did not reproduce it. That is grounds for a person to mark it resolved; it is not a resolution on its own.

objective: A resolved finding detected again is marked as a regression
preconditions: a baseline in which the real BOLA finding was resolved
input: The live scan compared against that baseline
expected: isRegression true and status Regressed, which the gate then fails at any severity
detail: 2 regression(s); gate FAIL

objective: A triage decision carries forward but the severity does not
preconditions: a baseline finding accepted at Medium, now detected at Critical
input: The same fingerprint with a higher severity in this scan
expected: The acceptance carries forward and the new severity is kept. A flaw that got worse since somebody accepted it should not inherit the old severity along with the decision
detail: status Accepted carried forward; severity Critical (was Medium)

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no justification
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses a false positive with no named decision-maker
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a false positive with no named decision-maker
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive with no named decision-maker. Somebody has to be accountable for a finding being set aside.

objective: Triage refuses a justification too short to be one
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: a justification too short to be one
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive: the justification is too short to be one. State what was checked and what it showed.

objective: Triage refuses an accepted risk with no justification
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: an accepted risk with no justification
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Refusing to mark BOLA as Accepted with no justification. A suppression with no stated reason is indistinguishable from turning the check off, and the gate counts it as open either way.

objective: Triage refuses an unknown status
preconditions: a confirmed finding from the live scan
input: an unknown status
expected: It throws. A suppression with no reason behind it is somebody switching the check off, and a workflow that accepts it quietly is how a gate becomes decoration
detail: Unknown security finding status 'Ignored'.

objective: A properly justified decision is accepted and appended to the history, never overwriting it
preconditions: a confirmed finding, marked a false positive with a reason and a name
input: A justification of substance and a named decision-maker, applied twice
expected: Both decisions in the history with the status each moved from. A status field that holds only the latest answer is not an audit trail
detail: Confirmed → NeedsReview, NeedsReview → FalsePositive

objective: A false positive suppresses that finding and not the same class elsewhere
preconditions: a BOLA finding marked a false positive on one endpoint
input: The suppression tested against the same category on a different endpoint
expected: It does not apply. Suppressing one endpoint's BOLA says something about that endpoint; applying it to every BOLA in the application would hide real ones
detail: applies to /api/accounts/{id}: yes; applies to /api/statements/{id}: false

objective: Self-healing cannot mark a security finding resolved
preconditions: the triage workflow
input: An attempt to resolve a finding with no person named
expected: Resolved requires a person, like every other status that stops a finding counting. The brief forbids self-healing hiding a security regression, and a machine-applied resolution is precisely that
detail: automated suppression refused (Refusing to mark BOLA as FalsePositive: the justification is...); an unreproduced finding stays Confirmed

objective: An application with no security scope returns 404, not an empty permissive scope
preconditions: an application nobody has authorized
input: GET the application's security scope
expected: 404. "Nobody has authorized this" and "there is a scope that allows nothing" are different facts, and returning a default-shaped object invites a caller to treat the first as configuration to tweak

objective: A scope cannot be enabled without a written authorization
preconditions: the application
input: A scope with enabled true and an empty authorization note
expected: 400, naming the field. Authorization is a written statement by a person, and the absence of a restriction is not permission
detail: 400: A security scope cannot be enabled without a written authorization. State who authorized security testing of this application, on whose behalf, and for what period.

objective: A scope cannot be enabled with an empty domain allowlist
preconditions: the application
input: A scope with a written authorization and no allowed domains
expected: 400. An empty allowlist permits nothing, and saving one as though it were a working scope hides that

objective: Destructive testing and production can never be authorized together

input: A scope with allowProduction and allowDestructiveTesting both true
expected: Refused as a security policy violation, at the point somebody tries to configure it rather than one request at a time later

objective: Reflection into a JSON body produces no XSS finding — it is not an HTML context

expected: No finding. Any finding here is a false positive on an endpoint that does nothing wrong
detail: element:not-html, attribute:not-html, script-tag:not-html

expected: No finding. Any finding here is a false positive on an endpoint that does nothing wrong

expected: No finding. Any finding here is a false positive on an endpoint that does nothing wrong
